title: Non-bipartite dense graphs contain a triangle
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph that is not bipartite, with $n$ vertices and $m$ edges. If \[(n-1)^2 + 4 < 4m,\] equivalently $m > \tfrac{(n-1)^2}{4} + 1$, then $G$ contains a triangle, i.e. three pairwise adjacent vertices. (Erdős)
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite simple graph
edge count m satisfies (n-1)^2 + 4 < 4m where n is the number of vertices
replaced:
\emph{.  }If \texttt{G} is simple and not bipartite with
\texttt{$\varepsilon$ > ($\nu$-1)$^{2}$/4 + 1}, then \texttt{G} contains a triangle.*

((\nu-1)^2/4)+1$, then $G$ contains a triangle. (P. Erd\"os)
